lines.text: Today you will learn a shortcut that programmers use all the time.
Climbing stairs is step, step, step. A square is a side and a turn, four times.
When you see a pattern, you can use a loop.
Both of these scripts draw a square.
The one on the right uses a repeat loop. It is shorter, and easier to read and change.
Here Pip climbs the stairs with a loop.
The four blocks inside the loop run, then run again, and again: three times.
Pip reaches the top with only five blocks!
With the pen, loops draw shapes.
For a triangle, repeat three times and turn 120 degrees.
The turns always add up to 360 degrees — one full turn.
Fantastic! Now try loops in the Code Lab and the puzzles.
